question.text: A primary aliphatic amine on reaction with nitrous acid in cold <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><mn>273</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></mrow></mfenced></math> and there after raising temperature of reaction mixture to room temperature <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><mn>298</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></mrow></mfenced></math>, gives a/an

solution.text:
A primary aliphatic amine on reaction with nitrous acid in cold gives a diazonium salt, but diazonium salt of aliphatic amines are not much stable, so, they dissociate on increasing temperature slightly and gives alcohol with water.

R-NH2→273°CHNO2aqRN2+→H2O283°CR-OH+N2
